• Namespace: guacamole
  • Sync Wave: Wave 7
  • Ingress Endpoint: https://guacamole.lambertlab.us
  • Architectural Role: Clientless HTML5 remote desktop gateway providing browser-based RDP and SSH access.
  • Key Configuration:
  • Multus CNI secondary interface net1 attached to vms/ovn-ad-vpc via dynamic DHCP allocation for direct wire-speed VM access.
  • InitContainer automated injection of internal Active Directory Root CA into Java truststore (cacerts).
  • Dual authentication chaining via EXTENSION_PRIORITY: "*,openid", supporting Microsoft Entra ID OIDC SSO while preserving local guacadmin emergency recovery.
  • Backend PostgreSQL database running on Longhorn distributed storage with longhorn-retain policy.
  • guacd resource limit (cpu: 2000m) preventing thread pool exhaustion on 32-thread Xeon compute nodes.

docs.title: Runbook: L2 Bridge Watchdog Self-Healing (Legacy)
docs.text:
[!NOTE] Archived Architectural Reference: This runbook is retained for historical and troubleshooting reference. The cluster has migrated from the NMState Linux host bridge (br-lab0) to the Kube-OVN Software-Defined L2 VPC (ovn-ad-vpc), which uses Geneve UDP encapsulation. Because Kube-OVN operates in user-space/OVS rather than enslaving physical host NICs into Linux bridges, asynchronous USB NIC boot latency issues and bridge carrier drops have been permanently eliminated, and the bridge-watchdog DaemonSet is no longer deployed.

This runbook covers the background, diagnosis, and automated self-healing architecture previously utilized for the br-lab0 multicast VXLAN bridge network.

docs.title: ⚠️ The Problem: USB NIC Boot Latency & Bridge Carrier Loss
Symptoms
docs.text: After physical node reboots (specifically on worker nodes like opti74), virtual machines and pods communicating across the 10.10.0.0/24 subnet reported loss of connectivity: * Apache Guacamole failed to connect to Windows 11 (win11-01.ad.lambertlab.us:3389). * CoreDNS forwarders timed out reaching dc01.ad.lambertlab.us (10.10.0.10).

docs.title: Root Cause Diagnosis
docs.text: When opti74 reboots, its external USB 3.0 Ethernet adapter (enx00e04c68b94d) enumerates asynchronously in the Linux kernel. If NetworkManager / NMState applies bridge policies before the USB controller has fully established physical link carrier: 1. br-lab0 enters a NO-CARRIER / DOWN state. 2. The virtual tunnel endpoint vxlan-lab becomes detached from master br-lab0. 3. Because NetworkManager does not continuously retry enslavement, the node remains severed from the L2 broadcast domain indefinitely.

docs.title: 🛠️ Automated Solution: bridge-watchdog DaemonSet
docs.text: To prevent manual intervention after reboots, a lightweight Kubernetes DaemonSet continuously polls link enslavement across all Linux nodes.

docs.title: Live Manifest
docs.text:
The documentation below is embedded directly from the repository source file:

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: bridge-watchdog
  namespace: kube-system
  labels:
    app: bridge-watchdog
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: bridge-watchdog
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: bridge-watchdog
    spec:
      hostNetwork: true
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/os: linux
      tolerations:
        - operator: Exists
      containers:
        - name: watchdog
          image: busybox:1.37
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tz-config
              mountPath: /etc/localtime
              readOnly: true
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              while true; do
                if ! ip link show vxlan-lab 2>/dev/null | grep -q "master br-lab0"; then
                  echo "$(date): Re-attaching vxlan-lab to br-lab0"
                  ip link set vxlan-lab master br-lab0
                  ip link set br-lab0 up
                fi
                sleep 15
              done
      volumes:
        - name: tz-config
          hostPath:
            path: /etc/localtime

docs.title: 🔍 How It Works
docs.text:
1. Host Network & Privileges: Runs with hostNetwork: true and privileged: true to access host network namespaces.
  2. Deterministic Check: Every 15 seconds, the watchdog inspects the kernel interface status: 
    ip link show vxlan-lab | grep "master br-lab0"
  3. Automated Re-Enslavement: If vxlan-lab is found un-enslaved, the container immediately executes: 
    ip link set vxlan-lab master br-lab0
ip link set br-lab0 up
  4. Zero Overhead: Employs Alpine BusyBox (1.37). It remains completely silent when healthy to prevent log spam, emitting timestamps matching the host's /etc/localtime.

docs.title: Runbook: Disaster Recovery & Cluster Quorum Restoration
docs.text: This runbook defines cold-boot boot sequencing, etcd Raft quorum recovery, KubeVirt virtual machine restoration, and emergency break-glass administrative procedures for the LambertLab infrastructure.

docs.title: ⚡ Deterministic Cold-Boot Boot Sequencing
docs.text:
Following a whole-home power failure or physical infrastructure maintenance, nodes must be booted in strict deterministic order to satisfy cross-service dependencies:

Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom 
graph TD
    Step1["Step 1: Storage Appliance<br/>TerraMaster F4-425 Plus (san.lambertlab.us)<br/>Wait 2-3 mins for iSCSI/NFS ready"] --> Step2["Step 2: Primary Control Plane Manager<br/>lenovo (etcd quorum member #1)<br/>Initializes kubeadm API server & kube-vip"]
    Step2 --> Step3["Step 3: Secondary Quorum Members<br/>optiplex & opti74 (etcd members #2 & #3)<br/>Restores Raft quorum & Cilium eBPF"]
    Step3 --> Step4["Step 4: Dedicated Compute Engine<br/>workstation (GPU & ECK Elastic Stack)<br/>Starts Elasticsearch NVMe engine"]
    Step4 --> Step5["Step 5: Virtual Machine Verification<br/>KubeVirt mounts SAN iSCSI LUNs<br/>DC01, Win11, OPNsense boot"]

docs.title: Stage 1: Storage Appliance (TerraMaster F4-425 Plus)
docs.text: Power on the NAS appliance first and wait until storage daemons initialize (~2–3 minutes): * Verify TCP port 3260 (iSCSI target daemon) is listening. * Verify NFS exports (/Volume3/isos, /Volume1/data) are accepting mount requests. * Failure Risk: Booting Kubernetes nodes before SAN targets are online causes KubeVirt PVC mounts to enter FailedMount or CrashLoopBackOff.

docs.title: Stage 2: Manager Node (lenovo)
docs.text:
Power on lenovo. The kubelet systemd service boots and automatically initializes the static control plane pods (etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, and kube-vip) from /etc/kubernetes/manifests/: * Check kubelet service status: 

sudo systemctl status kubelet
* Verify control plane static pods are running: 
sudo crictl ps | grep -E "kube-apiserver|etcd|kube-vip"

docs.title: Stage 3: Secondary Control Plane Members (optiplex & opti74)
docs.text:
Power on optiplex and opti74 simultaneously: * Once a second node joins, etcd re-establishes a majority quorum ($2/3$ members), and the Kubernetes API server begins accepting workload requests. * Verify node cluster status: 

kubectl get nodes -o wide

docs.title: Stage 4: Heavy Compute Engine (workstation)
docs.text:
Power on workstation: * The node kubelet connects to the control plane. * Docker engine starts local GPU media workloads (Jellyfin transcoding, Tdarr pipelines). * The Kubernetes control plane / ECK operator resumes the in-cluster Elastic Stack workloads on workstation, re-binding the local NVMe PersistentVolume (elasticsearch-data-pv) to initialize elasticsearch-es-default-0, logstash-ls-0, and fleet-server-agent with GELF listening on port 12201. * Verify Elastic Stack pods reach Running status: 

kubectl get pods -n observability -o wide

docs.title: ⚖️ etcd Raft Quorum Loss & Recovery
docs.text: If two of the three control plane nodes suffer permanent hardware loss, etcd will lose Raft consensus and the API server will reject all write requests.

docs.title: Single Node Quorum Re-seeding (Disaster Recovery)
docs.text:
If only lenovo survives catastrophic hardware loss on optiplex and opti74, re-bootstrap etcd as a single-node cluster:

  1. Edit the static pod manifest for etcd on lenovo: 
    sudo nano /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml
  2. Add the flag --force-new-cluster to the etcd command arguments in the manifest.
  3. Kubelet will automatically restart the etcd pod and force a new single-member consensus quorum.
  4. Once the API server is healthy and accepting requests, remove --force-new-cluster from /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml so normal consensus operations resume.
  5. Re-join replacement control plane nodes using kubeadm join 10.0.0.201:6443 --control-plane.

docs.title: 🖥️ KubeVirt Virtual Machine Restoration
docs.text:
If virtual machines fail to resume automatically after a host reboot:

  1. Inspect active VM status across the vms namespace: 
    kubectl get vms -n vms
kubectl get vmis -n vms
  2. Start any stopped virtual machines: 
    virtctl start dc01 -n vms
virtctl start win11 -n vms
  3. Verify underlying iSCSI SAN disk attachments: 
    kubectl describe vmi win11 -n vms | grep -A 10 "Volumes"
  4. Access direct out-of-band graphical consoles via VNC if guest OS networking fails: 
    virtctl vnc win11 -n vms

docs.title: 🔑 Break-Glass Administrative Procedures
docs.text:
In the event of a catastrophic directory or federation failure:

Failure Scenario Emergency Access Vector Operational Procedure On-Prem DC01 Failure Microsoft Entra ID Cloud Admin Log into Azure / Entra portal using the emergency break-glass account (pure cloud Global Admin). Independent of on-premises AD or Kerberos. Entra ID / Internet Outage On-Premise Domain Admin Access dc01 or win11 console directly via virtctl vnc using LAMBERTLAB\chris or the local machine administrator account. Guacamole SSO Unavailable Local guacadmin Account Browse to https://guacamole.lambertlab.us. Because EXTENSION_PRIORITY: "*,openid" is configured, local DB authentication runs first. Log in directly with guacadmin. Vault Sealed on Reboot Vault Unseal Keys If Vault unsealing is interrupted, execute vault operator unseal using the recovery Shamir unseal keys stored in the physical offline safe.

docs.title: Runbook: Docker to ECK Operator Migration & Elastic AutoOps Cloud Connect

docs.title: 🏛️ Architectural Overview & Transformation
docs.text:
Prior to migration, Elasticsearch 8.x, Logstash, and Fleet Server ran as standalone Docker containers on the workstation node. While functional, this introduced manual operational overhead, unmanaged TLS certificates, and lack of GitOps lifecycle management.

docs.title: 📋 Procedure 1: Backup & 50MB Config-Only Snapshot
docs.text: To migrate all dashboards, saved searches, detection rules, alerts, and Fleet policies without copying 35+ GB of ephemeral container logs, a config-only snapshot was created.

docs.title: 1.1 Snapshot Parameter Specification
docs.text:
PUT _snapshot/migration_repo/homelab_config_v1?wait_for_completion=true
{
  "indices": ".kibana*,.fleet*,.security*",
  "include_global_state": true,
  "feature_states": ["kibana", "fleet"]
}
  • indices: Captures .kibana* (~36 MB, 58 dashboards, 42 saved searches, Lens visualizations), .fleet* (agent policies), and .security* (API keys, service tokens, roles). Completely excludes data streams (homelab-logs-*, .ds-metrics-*).
  • include_global_state: Preserves cluster metadata, index templates, and Index Lifecycle Management (ILM) retention policies.
  • feature_states: Ensures transactional consistency for system indices during snapshot and restore.

docs.title: 1.2 Preparation on Workstation
docs.text:
Create host directories with proper UID ownership: 

ssh workstation "sudo mkdir -p /home/chris/services/elasticsearch/data /home/chris/services/elasticsearch/snapshots && sudo chown -R 1000:1000 /home/chris/services/elasticsearch/data /home/chris/services/elasticsearch/snapshots"

docs.title: 1.3 Register Repository & Execute Snapshot in Docker
docs.text:
1. Mount /home/chris/services/elasticsearch/snapshots to /usr/share/elasticsearch/snapshots in the Docker Elasticsearch container and configure path.repo: /usr/share/elasticsearch/snapshots.
  2. Register the snapshot repository: 
    curl -X PUT "http://100.106.96.18:9200/_snapshot/migration_repo" \
  -u elastic:<elastic_password> \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "type": "fs",
    "settings": {
      "location": "/usr/share/elasticsearch/snapshots",
      "compress": true
    }
  }'
  3. Trigger the snapshot: 
    curl -X PUT "http://100.106.96.18:9200/_snapshot/migration_repo/homelab_config_v1?wait_for_completion=true" \
  -u elastic:<elastic_password> \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "indices": ".kibana*,.fleet*,.security*",
    "include_global_state": true,
    "feature_states": ["kibana", "fleet"]
  }'
  4. Verify snapshot state: 
    curl -s -u elastic:<elastic_password> "http://100.106.96.18:9200/_snapshot/migration_repo/homelab_config_v1" | jq '.snapshots[0].state'
# Expected output: "SUCCESS"

docs.title: 🚀 Procedure 2: Deploying ECK Elasticsearch to Kubernetes
2.1 PersistentVolume Configuration (kubernetes/observability/elasticsearch/storage.yaml)
docs.text:
A dedicated PersistentVolume locks the local NVMe storage to the exact pod instance: 

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: elasticsearch-data-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 100Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath:
    path: /home/chris/services/elasticsearch/data
  nodeAffinity:
    required:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
            - key: kubernetes.io/hostname
              operator: In
              values:
                - workstation
  claimRef:
    namespace: observability
    name: elasticsearch-data-elasticsearch-es-default-0

docs.title: 2.2 Preserving the Master Password via Vault (external-secrets.yaml)
docs.text:
An ExternalSecret retrieves the existing elastic_password from HashiCorp Vault (secret/data/homelab) and provisions elasticsearch-es-elastic-user so the operator preserves the established master password: 

---
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: elasticsearch-es-elastic-user
  namespace: observability
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: vault-backend
  target:
    name: elasticsearch-es-elastic-user
    creationPolicy: Owner
    template:
      engineVersion: v2
      data:
        elastic: "{{ .elastic_password }}"
  data:
    - secretKey: elastic_password
      remoteRef:
        key: secret/data/homelab
        property: elastic_password

docs.title: 2.3 Elasticsearch Custom Resource (elasticsearch.yaml)
docs.text: Key configurations include: * node.store.allow_mmap: false: Bypasses the strict vm.max_map_count >= 262144 check, allowing unprivileged execution without requiring a privileged host-level sysctl initContainer. * path.repo: [/mnt/snapshots]: Mounts the host snapshot folder. * 16GB Heap: Configured via ES_JAVA_OPTS="-Xms16g -Xmx16g" backed by 20Gi container memory limit.

docs.title: 🔄 Procedure 3: Restoring the Snapshot into ECK
docs.text:
Once elasticsearch-es-default-0 is in Running state:

  1. Register the repository in ECK: 

    ES_PASS=$(kubectl get secret elasticsearch-es-elastic-user -n observability -o jsonpath="{.data.elastic}" | base64 -d)
kubectl run es-init --rm -it --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl -n observability -- \
  curl -k -X PUT "https://elasticsearch-es-http:9200/_snapshot/migration_repo" \
  -u "elastic:$ES_PASS" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "type": "fs",
    "settings": {
      "location": "/mnt/snapshots"
    }
  }'

  2. Restore the configuration snapshot: 

    kubectl run es-restore --rm -it --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl -n observability -- \
  curl -k -X POST "https://elasticsearch-es-http:9200/_snapshot/migration_repo/homelab_config_v1/_restore?wait_for_completion=true" \
  -u "elastic:$ES_PASS" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "indices": ".kibana*,.fleet*,.security*",
    "include_global_state": true
  }'

  3. Strip replica requirements across restored indices to maintain GREEN cluster status on a single node: 

    curl -k -X PUT -u "elastic:$ES_PASS" "https://es.lambertlab.us/*/_settings" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "index": {
      "number_of_replicas": 0
    }
  }'

docs.title: 4.1 Kibana Association (kibana.yaml)
docs.text:
Configured with native operator association: 

spec:
  version: 9.3.2
  count: 1
  elasticsearchRef:
    name: elasticsearch
  config:
    server.publicBaseUrl: "https://kibana.lambertlab.us"
    logging.root.level: "warn"
The operator automatically provisions service accounts and mutual TLS certificates between Kibana and Elasticsearch.

docs.title: 4.2 Logstash Ingestion via HostNetwork 12201 (logstash.yaml)
docs.text:
To ingest container logs from all Docker daemons over the Tailscale network without modifying Docker daemon logging configs, Logstash runs directly on the workstation host network with hostNetwork: true: 

podTemplate:
  spec:
    hostNetwork: true
    dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet
    nodeSelector:
      kubernetes.io/hostname: workstation
    containers:
      - name: logstash
        ports:
          - name: gelf-udp
            containerPort: 12201
            protocol: UDP
          - name: gelf-tcp
            containerPort: 12201
            protocol: TCP
By utilizing hostNetwork: true, Logstash binds to all physical and virtual interfaces (including tailscale0 at 100.106.96.18:12201), while dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet preserves in-cluster DNS resolution for CoreDNS and Kubernetes services (elasticsearch-es-http.observability.svc). Incoming logs are tagged with received_at and indexed directly into logstash-%{+YYYY.MM.dd} with number_of_replicas: 0.

docs.title: 🛡️ Procedure 5: Fleet Server & Agent Ingress Architecture
5.1 The Kube-OVN HostNetwork Caveat
docs.text:
Homelab host agents (agent-pernode-elastic-agent) run with hostNetwork: true to capture bare-metal network, system, and kernel metrics. Because Kube-OVN isolates the overlay network, host-networked pods cannot route across nodes to Kubernetes ClusterIPs (10.96.0.0/12).

Resolution: Agents route to Fleet Server and Elasticsearch via Traefik Ingress: * Fleet Endpoint: https://fleet.lambertlab.us * Elasticsearch Endpoint: https://es.lambertlab.us

docs.title: 5.2 Traefik Backend Insecure Transport
docs.text:
Because ECK generates internal self-signed backend certificates, Traefik must communicate with the backend services using an insecure transport: 

---
apiVersion: traefik.io/v1alpha1
kind: ServersTransport
metadata:
  name: insecure-transport
  namespace: observability
spec:
  insecureSkipVerify: true
Secondary services (fleet-server-agent-http-service and elasticsearch-es-http-service) in observability reference this transport: 
annotations:
  traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/service.serversscheme: https
  traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/service.serverstransport: observability-insecure-transport@kubernetescrd

docs.title: 5.3 Purging Stale Fleet API Keys
docs.text:
Restoring .kibana from the standalone Docker snapshot restores legacy API keys named Default that Elasticsearch does not recognize. Purge the stale keys via the Kibana Fleet API so Fleet Server generates valid active enrollment tokens: 

curl -sk -u "elastic:$ES_PASS" -X DELETE "https://kibana.lambertlab.us/api/fleet/enrollment_api_keys/<stale_key_id>" \
  -H "kbn-xsrf: true"

docs.title: 🧹 Procedure 6: Decommissioning Docker Resources
docs.text:
Once the ECK stack is validated:

  1. Target-destroy Docker ELK containers and resources on workstation: 

    terraform -chdir=terraform destroy \
  -target=module.docker_apps.docker_container.elasticsearch \
  -target=module.docker_apps.docker_container.logstash \
  -target=module.docker_apps.docker_container.fleet_server \
  -target=module.docker_apps.docker_image.elasticsearch \
  -target=module.docker_apps.docker_image.logstash \
  -target=module.docker_apps.docker_network.elk_bridge

  2. Move Terraform manifests into docker/archived/ using git mv: 

    git mv docker/workstation/app-elasticsearch.tf docker/archived/
git mv docker/workstation/app-logstash.tf docker/archived/
git mv docker/workstation/app-fleet-server.tf docker/archived/

  3. Remove decommissioned variables from docker/workstation/variables.tf, terraform/main.tf, and terraform/vault.tf.

docs.title: ☁️ Procedure 7: Elastic AutoOps Cloud Connect
docs.text: Elastic AutoOps provides cloud-hosted diagnostic insights and proactive shard analysis for self-managed clusters.

docs.title: 7.1 Architecture & Kustomize Deployment
docs.text:
Instead of managing large static manifests or embedding plaintext secrets in Helm values, AutoOps is deployed via remote Kustomize in kubernetes/observability/autoops/:

---
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: autoops-agents
resources:
  - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elastic/autoops-install/main/k8s/autoops_agent_deployment.yaml
  - external-secrets.yaml
  • Image: docker.elastic.co/elastic-agent/elastic-otel-collector-wolfi:9.4.3 (OpenTelemetry Collector with built-in otel_samples/autoops_es.yml).
  • Vault Integration: Sensitive cloud tokens (autoops_token, elastic_cloud_connected_mode_api_key, temp-resource-id, es_password) are stored in Vault under secret/data/autoops and mapped into autoops-secret via ExternalSecret with creationPolicy: Owner.
  • Telemetry Route: Scrapes diagnostics locally from https://es.lambertlab.us and exports OTLP metrics over HTTPS to Elastic Cloud (https://otel-auto-ops.us-east-2.aws.svc.elastic.cloud).

docs.title: 7.2 Verification
docs.text:
Verify the agent has successfully registered: 

kubectl logs -n autoops-agents deployment/autoops-elastic-agent --tail=20
Expected output confirms cluster registration: 
Registered cluster <cluster_id> for Cloud Connect: <resource_id>
autoops_es.cat_shards: success
autoops_es.cluster_health: success
events: acked by Elastic Cloud AutoOps
Access the resulting insights directly on cloud.elastic.co under Deployments > AutoOps.

docs.title: Runbook: Elastic Stack & Single-Node Index Lifecycle Management (ILM)
docs.text: This runbook documents operational maintenance, health verification, Index Lifecycle Management (ILM) policies, and troubleshooting procedures for the LambertLab centralized Elastic Stack (ELK: Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) running on Kubernetes under the ECK Operator (v3.5.0) in the observability namespace.

docs.title: ⚠️ The Problem: Single-Node Elasticsearch Cluster Health (YELLOW)
Symptoms
docs.text:
• Elasticsearch cluster health reports status: "yellow": 
    curl -sk -u elastic:<elastic_password> "https://es.lambertlab.us/_cluster/health?pretty"
  • Output displays unassigned_shards > 0.
  • Automated Index Lifecycle Management (ILM) policies fail to advance indices from Hot to Warm, Cold, or Delete phases.
  • Indices accumulate indefinitely, leading to disk space exhaustion on workstation local NVMe storage.

docs.title: Root Cause Diagnosis
docs.text: By default, Elasticsearch index templates configure indices with number_of_replicas: 1. In a single-node cluster (configured with discovery.type=single-node), there is only one node (workstation). Elasticsearch refuses to allocate a replica shard on the same physical node as the primary shard, leaving the replica permanently unassigned. Because the cluster cannot fulfill its replica policy, its health status degrades to YELLOW, causing ILM retention and rollover automation to stall.

docs.title: Step 1: Update Existing Indices Immediately
docs.text:
Run the following REST command to immediately strip replica requirements across all active indices:

curl -sk -X PUT -u elastic:<elastic_password> "https://es.lambertlab.us/*/_settings" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "index": {
      "number_of_replicas": 0
    }
  }'

Within seconds, the unassigned shards will clear and cluster health will transition to GREEN:

curl -sk -u elastic:<elastic_password> "https://es.lambertlab.us/_cluster/health?pretty" | grep "status"
# Expected output: "status" : "green"

docs.title: Step 2: Configure Global Component Template for Future Indices
docs.text:
To ensure all future daily indices (homelab-logs-YYYY.MM.dd, logstash-*) are created with zero replicas out of the box, apply a high-priority index template:

curl -sk -X PUT -u elastic:<elastic_password> "https://es.lambertlab.us/_index_template/homelab_single_node_template" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "index_patterns": ["homelab-logs-*", "logstash-*", "*"],
    "priority": 500,
    "template": {
      "settings": {
        "number_of_shards": 1,
        "number_of_replicas": 0,
        "refresh_interval": "5s"
      }
    }
  }'

docs.title: 1. Verifying Docker GELF over Tailscale (Port 12201)
docs.text:
To test whether Logstash is actively accepting GELF logs over the Tailscale network mesh, send a test payload using Netcat from any cluster node (lenovo, optiplex, or opti74):

# Send a test GELF UDP packet to Logstash on workstation
echo '{"version": "1.1", "host": "test-node", "short_message": "GELF test ping", "level": 6}' | nc -u -w 1 workstation 12201

Confirm ingestion by querying the most recent documents in Elasticsearch:

curl -sk -u elastic:<elastic_password> "https://es.lambertlab.us/logstash-*/_search?q=GELF+test+ping&pretty"

docs.title: 2. Inspecting Logstash Pipeline Status
docs.text:
Check ECK Logstash pod logs in Kubernetes:

kubectl logs -n observability logstash-ls-0 -f --tail 50
Healthy output should confirm active input on 0.0.0.0:12201 (GELF UDP/TCP) with zero pipeline worker exceptions.

docs.title: 💾 Disk Space Management & Data Pruning
docs.text:
• Storage Path: Dedicated workstation NVMe at /home/chris/services/elasticsearch/data bound via PersistentVolume elasticsearch-data-pv.
  • Prohibition: Never configure Elasticsearch data paths targeting 1Gbps network iSCSI or NFS shares.
  • Emergency Index Deletion: If workstation disk space drops below 15% and immediate pruning is necessary: 
    # Delete older logstash indices
curl -sk -X DELETE -u elastic:<elastic_password> "https://es.lambertlab.us/logstash-2026.08.*"

docs.title: Runbook: High-Speed Direct iSCSI Flashing (qemu-img)
docs.text: This runbook documents the procedure for flashing KubeVirt virtual machine boot disks directly to TerraMaster SAN iSCSI target LUNs at line-rate speed.

docs.title: The Traditional Bottleneck (CDI Uploads)
docs.text: Standard KubeVirt image uploads using virtctl image-upload route through the Kubernetes Containerized Data Importer (CDI) and the Traefik ingress controller: * CDI provisions an intermediate 64 GB Longhorn scratch volume on physical host SSDs. * Uploading large 25+ GB images triggers Traefik HTTP proxy idle timeouts (unexpected EOF). * Host disks are subjected to heavy write amplification and scratch volume allocation locks (Multi-Attach error for volume).

docs.title: The High-Speed Solution: libiscsi
docs.text: qemu-img natively supports user-space iSCSI protocols through libiscsi. By writing directly from the NAS template storage into the iSCSI block target LUN: * Zero scratch volumes are allocated on Kubernetes nodes. * Zero ingress timeouts because data transfers over a direct TCP socket. * Flashing completes in 2–3 minutes at full gigabit line rate.

docs.title: 1. Identify Target SAN LUN
docs.text: Ensure the target LUN is mapped on the TerraMaster SAN (san.lambertlab.us): * IQN: iqn.2026-09.us.lambertlab:win11-boot * LUN ID: 0

docs.title: 2. Execute Direct qemu-img convert
docs.text:
Run the conversion directly from the node with access to the template store:

qemu-img convert -p -f qcow2 -O raw \
  /mnt/nas-mount/templates/win11-template.qcow2 \
  iscsi://san.lambertlab.us/iqn.2026-09.us.lambertlab:win11-boot/0

docs.title: Flag Breakdown
docs.text:
• -p: Displays real-time percentage progress bar.
  • -f qcow2: Specifies input format (compressed QCOW2 template).
  • -O raw: Converts output directly to raw uncompressed block format on the LUN.
  • iscsi://...: Direct user-space iSCSI connection string bypassing host kernel iscsiadm initiator logins.

docs.title: 🔄 Post-Flash Boot Procedure
docs.text:
Once the flash completes: 1. Start or restart the KubeVirt virtual machine: 

virtctl start win11-01
2. Monitor boot console via VNC or serial console: 
virtctl vnc win11-01
3. Windows 11 will automatically execute the generalized Sysprep specialization phase using the declarative win11-unattend-secret.

docs.title: 🔒 Phase 1: Pre-Migration Safety & Backups
docs.text:
Before decommissioning the legacy K3s cluster, full application state and storage volumes were captured and verified:

  1. Longhorn Persistent Volume Snapshots: Targeted NFS storage appliance at nfs://10.0.0.60:/Volume4/longhorn:
  2. data-vault-0: Snapshot verified on NAS.
  3. data-guacamole-postgresql-0: Snapshot verified on NAS.
  4. cache-ntfy-0: Snapshot verified on NAS.
  5. HashiCorp Vault Raft Database Backup: Direct Raft engine snapshot saved to local administrative storage: 
    vault operator raft snapshot save /home/chris/cluster-backup-20261015/vault-backup.snap

docs.title: 🧹 Phase 2: Host Operating System Preparation (All Nodes)
1. Decommission Legacy K3s
docs.text:
Cleanly uninstall the K3s supervisor and purge stale CNI devices to prevent iptables/routing collisions:

# On worker nodes:
sudo /usr/local/bin/k3s-agent-uninstall.sh 2>/dev/null || sudo /usr/local/bin/k3s-uninstall.sh

# On control plane nodes:
sudo /usr/local/bin/k3s-uninstall.sh

# Purge leftover state and network interfaces:
sudo rm -rf /etc/rancher /var/lib/rancher /var/lib/kubelet /etc/cni /opt/cni /var/lib/cni
sudo ip link delete cni0 2>/dev/null
sudo ip link delete flannel.1 2>/dev/null

docs.title: 2. Kernel Modules & Sysctl Network Forwarding
docs.text:
Kubernetes and containerd require Linux bridge netfilter and IP packet forwarding:

cat <<EOF | sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/k8s.conf
overlay
br_netfilter
EOF

sudo modprobe overlay
sudo modprobe br_netfilter

cat <<EOF | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/k8s.conf
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables  = 1
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-ip6tables = 1
net.ipv4.ip_forward                 = 1
EOF

sudo sysctl --system

docs.title: 3. Upstream containerd Installation & Systemd Cgroups
docs.text:
Generate the default containerd configuration and enforce SystemdCgroup = true to match Kubernetes v1.37 cgroup requirements:

sudo mkdir -p /etc/containerd
containerd config default | sudo tee /etc/containerd/config.toml
sudo sed -i 's/SystemdCgroup = false/SystemdCgroup = true/g' /etc/containerd/config.toml

sudo systemctl restart containerd
sudo systemctl enable containerd

Verification: 

grep SystemdCgroup /etc/containerd/config.toml

docs.title: 4. Install Kubernetes Binaries (v1.37.1)
docs.text:
Pin the official community repository packages:

curl -fsSL https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.37/deb/Release.key | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes-apt-keyring.gpg
echo 'deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes-apt-keyring.gpg] https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.37/deb/ /' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kubernetes.list

sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y kubelet kubeadm kubectl
sudo apt-mark hold kubelet kubeadm kubectl

docs.title: 5. Explicit Kubelet Node IP Pinning
docs.text:
Homelab nodes frequently have multiple network interfaces (Tailscale tailscale0, Docker bridges, KVM virbr0, or secondary USB adapters). To prevent Kubelet from binding to the wrong interface, pin each node's physical LAN IP in /etc/default/kubelet:

  • lenovo: 
    echo 'KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS="--node-ip=10.0.0.11"' | sudo tee /etc/default/kubelet
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
  • optiplex: 
    echo 'KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS="--node-ip=10.0.0.12"' | sudo tee /etc/default/kubelet
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  • opti74: 
    echo 'KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS="--node-ip=10.0.0.13"' | sudo tee /etc/default/kubelet
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  • workstation: 
    echo 'KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS="--node-ip=10.0.0.14"' | sudo tee /etc/default/kubelet
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

docs.title: 6. NVIDIA GPU Runtime (Workstation Only)
docs.text:
On workstation, configure NVIDIA Container Toolkit CDI integration:

sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=containerd
sudo systemctl restart containerd
(Produces /etc/containerd/conf.d/99-nvidia.toml imported by containerd).

docs.title: 1. Stage kube-vip Static Pod Manifest
docs.text:
Deploy the floating control plane VIP (10.0.0.201) on interface eno1:

sudo mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/manifests
export VIP="10.0.0.201"
export INTERFACE="eno1"
export KVVERSION="v1.2.4"

alias kube-vip="sudo ctr image pull ghcr.io/kube-vip/kube-vip:$KVVERSION; sudo ctr run --rm --net-host ghcr.io/kube-vip/kube-vip:$KVVERSION vip /kube-vip"

kube-vip manifest pod \
  --interface $INTERFACE \
  --address $VIP \
  --controlplane \
  --services \
  --arp \
  --leaderElection | sudo tee /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-vip.yaml

[!IMPORTANT] Kubeconfig Volume Mount Note: In Kubernetes v1.29+ / v1.37, during the raw kubeadm init bootstrap phase prior to RBAC application, the volume mount in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-vip.yaml points to /etc/kubernetes/super-admin.conf on the host, while retaining mountPath: /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf inside the container.

docs.title: 2. Initialize Cluster with kubeadm-config.yaml
docs.text:
The cluster configuration disables kube-proxy and defines the pod subnet:

---
apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta4
kind: InitConfiguration
localAPIEndpoint:
  advertiseAddress: 10.0.0.11
  bindPort: 6443
nodeRegistration:
  criSocket: unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock
  imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  name: lenovo
  taints: []
---
apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta4
kind: ClusterConfiguration
kubernetesVersion: 1.37.1
clusterName: homelab-cluster
controlPlaneEndpoint: "10.0.0.201:6443"
networking:
  podSubnet: 10.244.0.0/16
  serviceSubnet: 10.96.0.0/12
  dnsDomain: cluster.local
proxy:
  disabled: true # Replaced completely by Cilium eBPF
etcd:
  local:
    dataDir: /var/lib/etcd

Run initialization on lenovo: 

sudo kubeadm init --config /home/chris/homelab/kubeadm-config.yaml --upload-certs

Set up user credentials: 

mkdir -p $HOME/.kube
sudo cp -i /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf $HOME/.kube/config
sudo chown $(id -u):$(id -g) $HOME/.kube/config

docs.title: 🌐 Phase 4: Cilium CNI in Pure eBPF Mode
docs.text:
Deploy Cilium via Helm using the official "Kubernetes Without kube-proxy" quick-start pattern:

helm repo add cilium https://helm.cilium.io/
helm repo update

helm install cilium cilium/cilium --version 1.20.3 \
  --namespace kube-system \
  --set kubeProxyReplacement=true \
  --set k8sServiceHost="10.0.0.201" \
  --set k8sServicePort="6443" \
  --set ipam.mode=kubernetes \
  --set hubble.relay.enabled=true \
  --set hubble.ui.enabled=true

docs.title: Architectural Decisions & Parameter Breakdown:
docs.text:
• kubeProxyReplacement=true: Directs Cilium eBPF programs to attach to socket layer and cgroups to manage ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer routing without iptables.
  • k8sServiceHost="10.0.0.201" & k8sServicePort="6443": Points Cilium agents directly to the kube-vip endpoint so agents can reach the API server prior to in-cluster service discovery availability.
  • ipam.mode=kubernetes (Critical): Cilium's default cluster-pool IPAM assigns 10.0.0.0/8, which conflicts with the physical 10.0.0.0/24 home LAN. Setting ipam.mode=kubernetes instructs Cilium to inherit the podSubnet: 10.244.0.0/16 delegated by Kubernetes (10.244.0.0/24 for lenovo, 10.244.1.0/24 for optiplex, etc.).
  • hubble.relay.enabled=true & hubble.ui.enabled=true: Deploys flow aggregation and web visualization.

docs.title: 1. Stage kube-vip.yaml on Secondary Nodes
docs.text:
Generate the manifest using the node's specific physical network interface. Note that secondary nodes use admin.conf directly:

  • On optiplex (interface eno1): 

    export VIP="10.0.0.201"
export INTERFACE="eno1"
export KVVERSION="v1.2.4"
alias kube-vip="sudo ctr image pull ghcr.io/kube-vip/kube-vip:$KVVERSION; sudo ctr run --rm --net-host ghcr.io/kube-vip/kube-vip:$KVVERSION vip /kube-vip"
sudo mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/manifests
kube-vip manifest pod --interface $INTERFACE --address $VIP --controlplane --services --arp --leaderElection | sudo tee /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-vip.yaml

  • On opti74 (interface enx00e04c68b94d): 

    export VIP="10.0.0.201"
export INTERFACE="enx00e04c68b94d"
export KVVERSION="v1.2.4"

sudo mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/manifests
kube-vip manifest pod --interface $INTERFACE --address $VIP --controlplane --services --arp --leaderElection | sudo tee /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-vip.yaml

docs.title: 2. Generate Control Plane Join Command
docs.text:
On lenovo: 

sudo kubeadm init phase upload-certs --upload-certs
# Output gives: <certificate-key>

kubeadm token create --print-join-command --certificate-key <certificate-key>

docs.title: 3. Execute Join
docs.text:
Run the generated join command with sudo on both optiplex and opti74: 

sudo kubeadm join 10.0.0.201:6443 \
  --token <token> \
  --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<hash> \
  --control-plane \
  --certificate-key <certificate-key>

[!NOTE] During join, etcd initially attaches the node as a non-voting "learner" while synchronizing Raft state. Transient warnings (etcdserver: can only promote a learner member which is in sync with leader) are expected for several seconds until the initial Raft log replication catches up.

docs.title: 🛠️ Phase 6: Joining Dedicated Worker Node (workstation)
docs.text:
Because workstation is a pure compute worker: * No kube-vip static pod is placed on workstation. * Worker join does not use --control-plane or --certificate-key.

Run on workstation: 

sudo kubeadm join 10.0.0.201:6443 \
  --token <token> \
  --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<hash>

Label the node role: 

kubectl label node workstation node-role.kubernetes.io/worker=worker

docs.title: 🚀 Phase 8: Next Steps (GitOps Reconciliation)
docs.text: With the foundation active, proceed to workload restoration: 1. Apply Cilium LoadBalancer IP Pool: Configure L2 announcements and reserve LAN IP blocks (e.g. 10.0.0.200/29) for Traefik ingress. 2. Restore Storage Engine (Longhorn CSI): Install Longhorn, bind nfs://10.0.0.60:/Volume4/longhorn, and restore persistent volume claims for Vault and Postgres. 3. Re-bootstrap Argo CD: Deploy Argo CD in manual sync mode to phase the GitOps rollout across sync waves.
